record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Can lunar-far-side 21 cm dark-ages telescopes such as LUSEE-Night and DSL detect PBH accretion imprints on diffuse hydrogen absorption against the cosmic microwave background out to redshifts below roughly 100, providing a high-redshift observational test of primordial black holes?

evidence.quote: Well before these telescopes are in action, there will be 21cm dark ages telescopes destined for the lunar far side, such as LUSEE-Night and DSL to probe PBH accretion imprints on diffuse hydrogen absorption against the CMB to z <∼ 100, both scheduled for deployment in 2026.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the cosmological 21 cm hydrogen absorption signal during the cosmic Dark Ages, measured as a differential brightness temperature of the diffuse neutral hydrogen against the cosmic microwave background (CMB) at redshifts in the range roughly 30 ≲ z ≲ 100. Suppose that a population of primordial black holes (PBHs) constitutes a fraction f_PBH of the dark matter, with masses in an astrophysically relevant window. Such PBHs accrete the ambient intergalactic medium and emit radiation that perturbs the gas kinetic temperature, the hydrogen spin temperature, and the ionization history, thereby imprinting a characteristic signature on the global 21 cm absorption signal and its power spectrum (including velocity acoustic oscillation features sourced by relative dark-matter–baryon streaming).

Question: Using lunar far-side radio interferometers/global-signal experiments operating in the frequency band corresponding to the redshifted 21 cm line from the Dark Ages (i.e., observing the cosmological 21 cm signal at z ≲ 100, free from Earth's ionosphere and terrestrial radio interference), is it possible to detect — at statistically significant level — the imprint of PBH accretion on the diffuse hydrogen 21 cm absorption signal against the CMB? Specifically, determine the range of PBH masses and abundances f_PBH for which such an experiment can either detect the accretion signature or place an upper limit improving on existing CMB-based constraints, accounting for instrumental sensitivity, foreground subtraction, and astrophysical uncertainties in the accretion model.
artifact.category_tag: 21 cm cosmology and primordial black holes
artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the detectability of PBH accretion imprints with future lunar far-side 21 cm Dark Ages experiments (LuSEE-Night, DSL), which are still in pre-deployment/early-operations stages. Recent forecasting work (e.g., on velocity acoustic oscillation features and PBH 21 cm forecasts) indicates the signature is in principle accessible, but astrophysical uncertainties significantly affect forecasts, and no measurement has yet been made. The problem is therefore open.

status_evidence.title: Primordial black holes and the velocity acoustic oscillations features in 21 cm signals from the cosmic Dark Ages
status_evidence.snippet: PBHs accrete ambient gas during the Dark Ages... VAO features could be a promising probe for detecting PBHs.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical forecasts suggest 21 cm Dark Ages signals could probe PBH accretion, but detection has not yet been achieved.

status_evidence.title: Astrophysical uncertainties challenge 21-cm forecasts: A primordial black hole case study
status_evidence.snippet: Astrophysical uncertainties challenge 21-cm forecasts for PBHs.
status_evidence.claim: Forecasting the PBH 21 cm signature remains uncertain due to astrophysical modeling.

status_evidence.title: LuSEE-Night Pathfinder Radio Telescope on the Far Side of the Moon
status_evidence.snippet: LuSEE-Night pathfinder mission for Dark Ages 21 cm measurement.
status_evidence.claim: LuSEE-Night is a pathfinder and has not yet produced PBH accretion measurements.
